newsitem.title: USA: U.S. concerned at continuing unrest in Albania.
newsitem.headline: U.S. concerned at continuing unrest in Albania.

text.p: The United States on Monday expressed concern about continuing unrest in Albania and told rebels holding parts of the country that Washington was firmly committed to the coalition government of the Balkan state.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the State Department was "deeply disturbed" by the actions of gunmen who ambushed Prime Minister Bashkim Fino on Saturday and prevented him from visiting the city of Shkoder.
"We call on all Albanians and all groups in Albania not to interfere in the process of reintegration and stabilisation and to pursue their concerns through a dialogue," Burns said.

He told reporters it was the responsibility of all Albanians to ensure the success of a government of national reconciliation formed last month by major Albanian political parties following an outbreak of lawlessness.

"The government enjoys broad international support that will not be affected by threats or unilateral withdrawals from the process by any of the individual political parties or groups inside Albania," Burns said. "The United States remains committed to working with this government."

The statement appeared designed to warn rebels who hold parts of southern Albania that they could hope for no international support. Unrest erupted in Albania following the collapse of popular investment schemes into which many had poured their savings.

Burns welcomed creation of a multinational force to protect aid supplies to Albania and praised Italy for leading it. Albania on Monday voiced concern over delays in deploying the force, now due to arrive next week.

But Burns said the primary responsibility lay with Albanians to restore order, establish conditions for free and fair elections and promote economic recovery. U.S. troops will not take part in the multinational force.
